 Delays in RTM projects will not be tolerated: Minister
 Andy Chua

 SIBU: The Communications Ministry will not tolerate contractors who fail to adhere to the implementation schedules of broadcasting infrastructure development projects in Sarawak, including the construction of RTM Sibu staff quarters, which is scheduled for completion on Sept 17, 2027.
 Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching stressed that compliance with technical specifications, construction quality standards and contractual timelines were mandatory requirements that contractors must take seriously.
 “The government will not compromise with contractors who fail to demonstrate commitment. Strict contract management measures, including the imposition of liquidated ascertained damages (LAD) and disciplinary action, will continue to be enforced,” she said.
 She was speaking during a working visit to the RTM Sibu staff quarters construction site here last night (Nov 26).
 On the project’s progress, Teo said the earlier delay was caused by soil conditions that necessitated deeper and additional piling work than initially estimated in the Bill of Quantities (BQ).
 She said the original specifications required piles to be driven to a depth of 21 metres at each point, but actual site conditions required depths of up to 48 metres.
 Following this, an Extension of Time (EOT) of 45 days was approved, with the revised completion date set for Sept 17, 2027.
 The project involves the construction of 16 residential units comprising 12 Class G units and four Class F units, designed as two-storey apartments.
 Teo said the provision of more comfortable, safe and conducive accommodation reflected the government’s concern for the welfare of RTM personnel, particularly those who worked far from their families and hometowns.
 In a related development, she said six RP1 extension development projects under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) were being implemented in Sarawak, comprising one project under the Information Department (JAPEN) and five under RTM.
 Of the six projects, five were currently under construction, while the RTM Kuching HD Studio upgrade was at the procurement or post-Letter of Acceptance (SST) stage.
 The five ongoing projects involved developments in Bintulu, Sibu, Sri Aman and Limbang, as well as the JAPEN Kuching extension building.
 She said the projects formed part of the government’s continuous efforts to strengthen digital broadcasting facilities and improve service coordination in northern Sarawak through the RTM Bintulu coordination centre.
 Teo said the working visit was aimed at monitoring the project’s progress and ensuring that construction proceeded smoothly in accordance with the approved specifications and contractual requirements.
 The project briefing was delivered by the Sarawak Public Works Department, the implementing agency.
 Also present was Sarawak Broadcasting Department director Wan Wizana Hashim.
